title: One-month baby checkup
what: A routine checkup at one month. The doctor checks how your baby is growing and developing.
why: For all babies at 1 month, on the checkup schedule.
duration: the pediatrician visit usually takes 20 to 30 minutes; longer if specialists or ultrasounds are needed
tell_doctor: How your baby feeds: breast, formula, or both
How they sleep, and how often they poop
If they spit up or cry a lot

prepare.title: Feeding
prepare.text: Feed your baby shortly before the visit, so they are calmer.

prepare.title: Things to bring
prepare.text: A blanket, a diaper, wipes, and a bottle if formula-fed.

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: Ask if other doctors or ultrasounds are needed that day.

bring: The medical record and vaccination record
steps: The nurse weighs your baby and measures length and head
The pediatrician checks the skin, soft spot, and belly
The doctor listens to the heart and lungs and checks reflexes
Sometimes you are referred to specialists or for an ultrasound
If a vaccine is due, it is discussed
The doctor gives advice on care and feeding
feel: Your baby may cry when undressed. That is normal
after: The next checkup is usually at 2 months
The pediatrician will explain ultrasound and specialist results
Vaccines follow the schedule your doctor gives
red_flags: Your baby is floppy or refuses to feed: call emergency services
A temperature over 38°C (100.4°F) in a baby under 3 months: call emergency services

faq.q: How much weight should my baby gain in a month?
faq.a: It varies. The doctor will judge the gain using growth charts and how your baby is doing.

faq.q: Why an ultrasound at one month?
faq.a: In some countries, the head, belly, and hips are checked at this age. Ask your pediatrician.

reminders.text: Your baby's one-month checkup is tomorrow. Bring the documents, a blanket, and your questions.
